title: Why Syria and Iraq are taking different approaches to armed groups
gist: Iraq under Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi broke with past practice by arresting people who desecrated the US flag during Sovereignty Day celebrations marking the Sept. 30, 2026 withdrawal of US-led coalition forces, drawing a backlash from the IRGC-backed Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba. The episode signals a Baghdad government testing its authority over Iran-aligned armed factions after Khamenei's death.

insights.claim: US-led coalition forces withdrew from Iraq on Sept. 30, 2026, an event marked in Iraq by Sovereignty Day celebrations.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: The end of the coalition presence removes a US security backstop and shifts Iraq's security balance toward domestic and Iran-aligned actors.
insights.quote: recent Sovereignty Day celebrations marking the Sept. 30 withdrawal of US-led coalition forces from the country

insights.claim: Unlike past practice, Iraq's government under Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly arrested several people for trampling and desecrating the US flag and ordered an inquiry, with several prominent Iraqi officials backing the disciplinary action.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Suggests the Zaidi government is signalling a pragmatic stance toward Washington and willingness to discipline anti-US activity.
insights.quote: Several people involved were reportedly arrested and an inquiry was ordered.
insights.locator: Iraq’s response under Prime Minister Ali

insights.claim: As of Oct. 8, 2026, Iraqi authorities had not publicly released the number, names, positions or affiliations of those arrested over the US flag desecration.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Opacity hints the government is avoiding direct confrontation with powerful factions whose members may be involved.
insights.locator: Iraq’s response under Prime Minister Ali

insights.claim: Akram al-Kaabi, commander of the IRGC-backed Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, denounced the Iraqi arrests over US flag desecration as a 'dangerous precedent' and posted an older video of himself walking on a US flag.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Open defiance by a major militia leader signals friction between Baghdad and Iran-aligned factions that could escalate.
insights.quote: railed against the “dangerous precedent” that the arrests had set, posting an older video of him walking on a US flag

insights.claim: Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, formed in 2013 and backed by Iran's IRGC, was among the first Iraqi factions to enter Syria to support Bashar al-Assad and played a major role in the battle for Aleppo.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Illustrates the cross-border reach of Iraqi militias, a channel for regional conflict spillover.
insights.locator: The paramilitary group is backed by

insights.claim: The US designated Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba a foreign terrorist organization on Sept. 19, 2025.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Sanctions exposure for any Iraqi entity or counterparty linked to the group.
insights.quote: It was designated a "foreign terrorist organization" by the US on Sept. 19, 2025.

insights.claim: In a 2015 interview, Akram al-Kaabi said his faction took orders from Iran's Ali Khamenei, would fight alongside Yemen's Houthis, and that Iran-linked Iraqi factions could overthrow the Iraqi government if Khamenei deemed it a religious duty.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: Shows militias' allegiance lies outside the Iraqi state, a structural risk to Iraqi political stability.

insights.claim: Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed by an Israeli airstrike in Tehran on Feb. 28, 2026, removing the figure Iran-linked Iraqi factions said they took orders from.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
insights.so_what: A decapitated chain of religious authority may weaken militias' cohesion and embolden Baghdad to assert control.
insights.quote: Khamenei was killed by an Israeli airstrike in Tehran on Feb. 28.
